coverage.method: Whole-text TF-IDF (1–2 grams, minimum document frequency 3) plus 42-component nonnegative matrix factorization, seeded 20261028; every full abstract included. Title/topic scan was a separate earlier pass.
limits: Clustering is not close reading of all broadcasts or proof of influence.
Catalogue and RSS coverage gaps retained from collector manifest.
Raw abstracts and per-document derived feature text are temporary and must be deleted after private mining.
coverage.manual_review_scope: Full substantive abstract text; contributor credits and reading lists generally omitted. No audio listened to.
coverage.supplemental_type: Collector-authored brief source-based synopses, not BBC verbatim abstracts

leads.title: The Library at Nineveh
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: The archive has a politics
leads.original_design_question: What makes scattered observations a body of knowledge? Put sky records, omen interpretation, scribal selection and royal power on the same desk.
leads.potential_connections: Archive -> comparison -> an argument about what survives.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: A physical royal astronomical/astrological report is documented; no claim that the whole collection was a modern public library.

leads.title: Cynicism
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: A philosophy can be a way of living
leads.original_design_question: Diogenes suggests an action rather than another summary: remove a social dependency and discover the freedom—and cost—of needing less.
leads.potential_connections: Socratic examination -> Cynic practice -> Stoic self-command; later luxury critique is a comparison unless sourced.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Anecdotes are transmitted literary evidence, not eyewitness transcripts.

leads.title: Aristotle's biology
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: Classification starts with living things
leads.original_design_question: Aristotle need not be only syllogisms. Compare animal structures and ask what a part does; later classification and evolution can change that explanation.
leads.potential_connections: Observed likeness -> kinds -> function -> adaptation.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Do not turn Aristotle into a modern evolutionary biologist or the first observer anywhere.

leads.title: The Music of the Spheres
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: Beauty can guide an explanation without proving it
leads.original_design_question: The attraction of a harmonious cosmos is a way to connect music, proportion and astronomy while keeping observations able to resist the beautiful model.
leads.potential_connections: Musical order -> celestial order -> Kepler’s revision rather than arithmetic drills.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Historical harmonic inquiry is not evidence that planets audibly sing.

leads.title: The Translation Movement
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: Translation changes the questions
leads.original_design_question: A manuscript crossing languages can acquire new problems and arguments rather than simply being carried like a sealed package.
leads.potential_connections: Greek texts + Syriac/Arabic scholarship -> original work -> Latin reception.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Separate Greek-to-Arabic and Arabic-to-Latin routes; do not credit a single building with every translation.

leads.title: The Needham Question
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: Question the shape of the history itself
leads.original_design_question: This is a design safeguard: ask what is hidden by a story that measures every tradition against a supposedly inevitable European endpoint.
leads.potential_connections: Paper, printing and other technical routes should disrupt a one-way ladder.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: The public abstract uses a strongly teleological framing; the game will not inherit its claim that Chinese inventions made little social difference. This lead is a research counterpoint, not an automatic chapter or geographic quota.

leads.title: The Science of Glass
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: Materials can reorganize knowledge
leads.original_design_question: A working craft can outrun a complete theory. Glass links lenses and instruments, but also asks whether useful making requires a finished explanation of the material.
leads.potential_connections: Craft -> lens -> distant/near worlds; many returns rather than a glass chapter quota.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: The abstract changed the lead: theory lagging technology is as important as optical applications. Glass must not be described as an ordinary liquid flowing slowly at room temperature.

leads.title: The Encyclopédie
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: Knowledge can be rearranged for readers
leads.original_design_question: The encyclopedic project offers a desk full of crafts and arguments with cross-references, and a live question about who gets to name the branches of knowledge.
leads.potential_connections: Workshop knowledge + print -> public reference work -> contested classifications.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: The complete historical source is available through an academic edition; game text will be authored, not bulk copied.

leads.title: Baconian Science
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: What did Francis Bacon actually change?
leads.original_design_question: Make the player notice a negative instance, isolate a variable, and organize collaborative inquiry. This is a substantive answer to the user’s question.
leads.potential_connections: Natural histories -> eliminative comparisons -> experiments -> cooperative research.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Bacon neither invented all experiment nor supplied the unique modern scientific method.

leads.title: Renaissance Magic
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: Magic and experiment need not be opposites
leads.original_design_question: A prestigious ancient-looking manuscript can redirect a Renaissance reader’s attention. Wonder, translation and the later dating of texts make a better tension than a simple magic-versus-science contest.
leads.potential_connections: Platonism -> Hermetic reading and natural magic; philology can alter the authority of a manuscript without making every idea in it disappear.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Hermetic transmission and dating still require specific sources before implementation; Della Porta is a related independently researched practice, not the same episode claim.

leads.title: The Invention of Photography
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: An image can become a trace
leads.original_design_question: A projected image plus a light-sensitive surface is an immediately intelligible synthesis. Its later effect on art and evidence need not be another measuring exercise.
leads.potential_connections: Camera obscura -> fixed photograph -> questions of framing, realism and art.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Photography has multiple inventors and processes; a fixed image is not automatically an objective interpretation.

leads.title: The Observatory at Jaipur
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: The sky is not a single European workshop
leads.original_design_question: Jaipur offers an active meeting of astronomical traditions and instruments, not an exotic interruption. Architecture itself can become an observing instrument.
leads.potential_connections: Translated tables + local observations + monumental instruments -> correction.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Verify the particular texts and people before asserting a direct transmission route.

leads.title: Longitude
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: A clock becomes a position
leads.original_design_question: Reference time and local noon make longitude conceptually graspable. Mechanical timekeepers and lunar observations remain alternative systems with different requirements.
leads.potential_connections: Astronomy + clocks + sea trials -> navigation; trade and coercion are not erased.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: No numerical longitude problem; no simple lone-genius versus foolish-establishment myth.

leads.title: Humboldt
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: A collection becomes a connected landscape
leads.original_design_question: Humboldt makes a different synthesis from taxonomy: altitude, climate and plant distribution can become a patterned whole.
leads.potential_connections: Specimen labels -> environmental relations -> ecology.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Recognize collaborators and local knowledge; do not present one European as discovering that nature is connected.

leads.title: Linnaeus
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: Names help—and can carry prejudice
leads.original_design_question: Classification creates a powerful shared tool but invites questions about which distinctions are useful and which rankings are imposed.
leads.potential_connections: Aristotelian kinds -> Linnaean naming -> evolutionary trees; human hierarchy remains criticizable.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Do not repeat historical racial classifications as biological truths.

leads.title: The Anatomy of Melancholy
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: The crowded desk can be the subject
leads.original_design_question: Burton is an antidote to sterile research summaries: inherited medicine, philosophy, literary examples and first-person experience gather in a deliberately sprawling book.
leads.potential_connections: Ancient temperaments -> Renaissance reading -> later questions about mind and interpretation.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Humoral explanations are historical positions, not present medical guidance.

leads.title: Relativity
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: Agreement does not require one universal clock
leads.original_design_question: Relativity can be reconstructed through light signals and differently moving observers, without formulas or confusing relativity with relativism.
leads.potential_connections: Operational time + light -> relative simultaneity -> spacetime.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Observer-dependent measurements are constrained, not arbitrary opinions.

leads.title: Bergson and Time
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: Measured time and lived time are different questions
leads.original_design_question: Bergson opens a genuine disagreement that need not be settled by one discipline defeating the other. Memory and anticipation can transform duration.
leads.potential_connections: Clock time versus experienced duration; comparison with fiction is a teaching juxtaposition unless documented.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Do not use lived duration to refute the empirical content of relativity.

leads.title: Surrealism
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: Ideas can be combined artistically
leads.original_design_question: Dream, chance and a familiar object in an impossible setting make an intelligible artistic operation. Freud, Marx and Dada are more fertile sources than “add art”.
leads.potential_connections: Optical realism + dream association -> a surreal image; reason does not simply vanish.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Freudian inspiration is documented; art does not prove psychoanalytic theories.

leads.title: Jorge Luis Borges
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: A library can become a philosophical machine
leads.original_design_question: Borges permits a genuinely different kind of combination: identical words in a changed context, a library with every possible book, a map that defeats its purpose.
leads.potential_connections: Earlier translation and textual criticism can return through creative translation, altered context, imaginary scholarship and possible worlds. These comparisons do not assert direct medieval-to-Borges influence.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: No quoted story text; no claim that Borges predicted quantum physics or the internet.

leads.title: Lévi-Strauss
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: Relations can matter more than isolated objects
leads.original_design_question: Lévi-Strauss is a direction for investigating how categories and contrasts organize meaning, with the limitations of the outsider’s scheme left visible.
leads.potential_connections: Classification -> relational structures -> contested universal patterns.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Specific structural claims and source communities need further primary-text verification.

leads.title: Nietzsche's Genealogy of Morality
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: Ask where a value came from
leads.original_design_question: Genealogy changes the question from whether a rule sounds timeless to how it acquired its authority and whom it serves.
leads.potential_connections: Inherited moral categories -> historical formation -> later critiques of knowledge and power.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Do not sanitize Nietzsche’s elitism or make genealogy equivalent to “all morality is false”.

leads.title: The Antikythera Mechanism
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: A model can be built into matter
leads.original_design_question: The Antikythera mechanism makes a powerful return of the oldest sky records: recurring celestial events represented in a working arrangement of gears.
leads.potential_connections: Recorded cycles -> mechanical model -> later clocks and computation, with gaps acknowledged.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Do not invent an unbroken device lineage to modern computers.

leads.title: The Fable of the Bees
leads.selection_basis: All 1,099 available full RSS abstracts computationally analyzed; this episode’s substantive abstract was also close-read
leads.hook: Private motives and public outcomes can diverge
leads.original_design_question: Mandeville creates a provocative counterweight to ancient virtue and later economic order. Keep prosperity, moral cost and distribution as separate questions.
leads.potential_connections: Luxury and self-interest -> unintended social effects; Smith is not just Mandeville with a new label.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Attributed controversial thesis, not proof that greed is good.

leads.title: Automata
leads.hook: When a mechanism looks alive
leads.original_design_question: A clock can animate a figure without explaining life. Let a convincing imitation generate a new question rather than automatically award the player a theory of mind.
leads.potential_connections: Ancient devices, Renaissance clocks, mechanical accounts of bodies, and future machines can return to the difference between representation and explanation.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Actual automata and astronomical displays are documented. Any continuity to later computing needs a separate source; apparent digestion must not be presented as real digestion.

leads.title: Malthusianism
leads.hook: An argument travels from society into biology
leads.original_design_question: A population argument meeting observed variation is a real cross-disciplinary turn, not a decorative borrowed manuscript. Its political implications must not be smuggled back as natural law.
leads.potential_connections: Malthus -> Darwin and Wallace; later mutual-aid arguments challenge a competition-only picture.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Wallace’s letter acknowledges both naturalists’ debt to Malthus. That does not validate every Malthusian policy or make evolution a moral prescription.

leads.title: William Morris
leads.hook: More production is not the only future
leads.original_design_question: A beautifully made object can conflict with miserable work. Morris lets the same industrial inheritance generate rival futures: more output, more leisure, or more control over making.
leads.potential_connections: Craft -> division of labour -> artistic and socialist criticism -> speculative workshop choices.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Use Morris’s actual argument about useful work; do not reduce him to nostalgia or a blanket rejection of machinery.

leads.title: Walter Benjamin
leads.hook: A reproduced image changes its social life
leads.original_design_question: The photographic branch need not end at a better picture. Copies that reach a crowd can change authority, access and political persuasion.
leads.potential_connections: Print -> photograph -> reproducible art -> public interpretation and propaganda.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Benjamin’s arguments about reproduction are historical theory, not a universal rule that copies destroy artistic value.

leads.title: Peter Kropotkin
leads.hook: Cooperation belongs inside the argument about life
leads.original_design_question: Keep mutual aid beside competition instead of forcing an evolutionary winner. The combination can change what a future community is designed to support.
leads.potential_connections: Natural selection -> disputed social readings -> mutual aid -> cooperative institutions as a speculative choice.
leads.research_scope_and_caution: Kropotkin’s argument is not a disproof of Darwin. Darwin did not reduce all living relations to combat; avoid that caricature.
